chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not quarrel with a forbearing one, nor with a foolish one, for the forbearing one would detest you and the foolish one would harm you.'

key_terms.يَقْلِيكَ: He will detest or tire of you
key_terms.يُؤْذِيكَ: He will harm or hurt you

ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid arguing with both wise and foolish people?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against disputing with both the forbearing (al-halim) and the foolish (al-safihi), as each poses a distinct risk: the former may tire of the argument or harbor silent resentment, while the latter causes direct harm through irrationality. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, highlights the Shia emphasis on strategic wisdom (hikmah) in social interactions, advising believers to preserve peace rather than win debates at the cost of relationships. It serves as a practical guide for navigating conflicts by understanding the psychological and behavioral traits of one's interlocutor.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Ammar Bin Marwan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not quarrel with a forbearing one nor with a foolish one, for the forbearing one would detest you and the foolish one would harm you’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindy from Ja’far ibn Bashir from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Do not engage in a disputation against either a forbearing or a thoughtless person; a forbearing person turns into your foe and a thoughtless person will hurt you.’”
